newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Gulf Canada makes hostile Clyde bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Gulf Canada makes hostile Clyde bid.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources on Wednesday launched a 432 million pound ($720 million) hostile bid for British oil firm Clyde Petroleum, but analysts believe the Canadian company will have to offer more to secure a deal.
Analysts noted the rise in Clyde's shares, which surged 33 pence to close at 118 pence, well above Gulf Canada's cash offer of 105 pence a share.
"The share price is telling you -- and I tend to agree -- that this bid is not going to be enough," said analyst Nick Antill at brokers BZW.
Clyde rejected the offer, saying it was "unsolicited and wholly unacceptable."
"This offer is far too low and anyway Clyde will continue to deliver better value to shareholders as an independent company," Clyde's chairman Malcolm Gourlay told Reuters.

Gulf Canada's bid, which propelled shares across Britain's oil production sector, comes hot on the heels of the $1.23 billion acquisition earlier this month of London-based Santa Fe Exploration by Norway's Saga Petroleum ASA.

"The offer for Clyde follows Gulf Canada's previously stated desire to increase its activities outside its existing core areas of North America and Indonesia," J. P. Bryan, president and chief executive of Gulf Canada said.
Clyde's North Sea and Australian assets would provide Gulf Canada with additional core areas, and Clyde's Indonesian assets would complement its existing assets, the Canadian firm said.

The company had earlier this year considered a bid for Australia's Command Petroleum Holdings NL, which instead became the takeover target of UK's Cairn Energy Plc . But Gulf Canada said last month Cairn's bid was too high to improve.
Consolidation in the worldwide exploration and production industry started about a year ago and follows half a decade of cost cutting, which has left many oil firms awash with cash.

Gulf Canada, which already owns 1.8 percent of Clyde, said its offer for Clyde represented a premium of 24.3 percent over the mid-market quotation for a Clyde share of 84 1/2 pence at close of trading on December 17.
Rising in Clyde's slipstream, Cairn Energy, which has promising activities in Bangladesh, jumped 21-1/2 pence to 411-1/2, while Hardy Oil & Gas Plc climbed 21 pence to 294.
Analysts said Gulf Canada's move could be a prelude to more takeover activity in the sector, adding that Gulf Canada's offer might well attract a counter bid.
"The whole industry is in a state of flux and certainly you cannot rule out another interested party," said Paul Spedding at Kleinwort Benson.
Gulf Canada plans an offering of its stock and a flotation of its Indonesian arm next year to help fund the proposed acquisition of Clyde.
Bryan told reporters in a conference call the company wanted to raise about $100 million from an offering of its stock in the U.S. and Canada early next year.
He said they were considering floating about 20 percent of the company's Indonesian arm, Asamera, late next year to raise $300 to $400 million.
Gulf Canada also plans to sell some $300 million in non-strategic assets throughout 1997. ($1=.6003 Pound)
